hero.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls to Just Three Vessels as Global Energy and Security Risks Persist
hero.description: Only three commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, while oil prices eased as Saudi Arabia expands alternative export routes. Meanwhile, Russian strikes hit Ukraine and Nigeria's Dangote IPO places heavy demand on digital investment platforms.

featured.title: Hormuz Traffic Falls to Three Vessels as Saudi Arabia Expands Alternative Oil Routes
featured.content: Preliminary tracking data recorded only three commercial vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, compared with 12 on Tuesday and a 10-day average of about 17. The figures underline the continuing disruption to one of the world's most important energy routes. However, oil prices have fallen as Saudi Arabia increases crude availability through alternative routes, including additional loadings from Oman's Sohar port. The data remains preliminary because vessels travelling with their tracking systems disabled may not be detected.
featured.imageQuery: Hormuz Strait oil tanker Oman Sohar port

articles.title: Hormuz Records Only Three Commodity Vessel Crossings
articles.content: Only three commercial commodity vessels were recorded crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to preliminary ship-tracking data. That compares with 12 crossings the previous day and a 10-day average of about 17. One vessel entered through an Iranian route, while two used routes that were not continuously visible to tracking systems. Analysts caution that AIS-based figures may undercount vessels deliberately operating without visible transponders.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker vessel satellite

articles.title: Oil Falls as Saudi Arabia Maintains Alternative Supply Routes
articles.content: Brent crude fell to around $104.33 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate to approximately $101.34 as concerns about an extended Saudi supply disruption eased. Saudi Arabia is increasing crude shipments through alternative arrangements, including additional loadings from Oman's Sohar port. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright has also indicated that restoration of Saudi's damaged East-West pipeline could occur sooner than initially feared.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia crude oil tanker Oman Sohar

articles.title: Diesel Markets Remain Under Pressure Despite Lower Oil Prices
articles.content: Falling crude prices have not removed pressure from refined fuel markets. European gasoil and U.S. ultra-low-sulfur diesel futures have reached record levels as disruptions affect Middle Eastern infrastructure and Russian refining capacity. A Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian refinery has added further uncertainty to diesel supplies.
articles.imageQuery: diesel fuel refinery European energy market

articles.title: Russia Launches Major Overnight Attack Across Ukraine
articles.content: Russia launched a large missile and drone attack against Kyiv and several other Ukrainian regions overnight. Ukrainian officials reported damage in eight regions, including energy infrastructure in Sumy and Odesa. Kyiv officials said 18 people were injured, including two children. Odesa reported six wounded after a 19-storey apartment building was damaged, while three people were injured in Zaporizhzhia after a missile strike hit industrial facilities and caused a fire.
articles.imageQuery: Kyiv Ukraine Russian drone missile attack damage

articles.title: U.S. House Passes Sweeping Russia and Iran Sanctions Bill
articles.content: The U.S. House of Representatives has approved a sweeping sanctions and tariff package intended to increase economic pressure on Russia and Iran. The legislation passed 262-159 and has been sent to President Donald Trump for consideration. The package includes sanctions affecting Russia's energy and defence sectors and provisions allowing tariffs on countries continuing certain purchases of Russian energy.
articles.imageQuery: US Capitol House of Representatives Washington

articles.title: Dangote IPO Demand Overwhelms Nigerian Investment Platforms
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO is generating unusually strong retail demand, with several digital investment platforms experiencing service disruptions. Reuters reported that one major platform recorded traffic around ten times its normal level within 30 minutes of the offer opening. The IPO is being promoted as a major opportunity for ordinary Nigerians to participate in the capital market.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote refinery Nigeria Lagos investment IPO

articles.title: Dangote IPO Offers Low Entry Point for Retail Investors
articles.content: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery public offer consists of 4.1 billion shares priced at ₦525 each. Investors can apply for a minimum of 10 shares, making the initial subscription ₦5,250 before applicable charges. The offer is scheduled to close on 13 October 2026 under the approved terms.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria stock market investment Lagos IPO

articles.title: SEC Warns Against Dangote IPO Fraud
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission is urging investors to remain cautious as interest in the Dangote IPO grows. Investors are being warned about fake websites, phishing attempts, impersonators and unauthorised payment requests. Prospective investors should independently confirm that any receiving agent or digital platform is authorised before providing money or personal information.

articles.title: Europe Pushes for Greater Strategic Security Cooperation
articles.content: European governments are discussing ways to strengthen the continent's ability to respond to security threats involving drones, sabotage, cyberattacks and other forms of hybrid activity. The discussions are taking place alongside wider efforts to strengthen European defence, energy security, industrial capacity and technology.
articles.imageQuery: European Union defence security meeting Brussels

articles.title: EU-Canada Partnership Proposal Gains Attention
articles.content: The European Union is considering a new associate-member relationship with Canada covering areas such as defence, energy, critical minerals, technology and supply chains. The proposal would not make Canada an EU member. Any new arrangement would require further negotiations and agreement among EU member states.
articles.imageQuery: Canada EU flags Ursula von der Leyen Mark Carney

articles.title: India Warns U.S. Measures Over Russian Oil Could Affect Relations
articles.content: India has warned that possible U.S. tariffs connected to countries buying Russian oil could affect bilateral relations. New Delhi says it remains focused on protecting its energy security and economic interests. India is one of the world's major oil importers and remains an important buyer of Russian crude.
articles.imageQuery: India Russia oil energy trade flags

articles.title: Experts Call for Stronger Safeguards Around Advanced AI
articles.content: Security experts from the United States and China are calling for stronger safeguards around increasingly autonomous artificial-intelligence systems, particularly where AI could interact with nuclear command systems or military cyber operations. Their recommendations include human oversight, defined limits and direct communication channels for AI-related incidents. The proposals have not been formally adopted by either government.

articles.title: Global Supply Chains Remain Exposed to Geopolitical Disruption
articles.content: The continuing disruption around Hormuz, pressure on refined-fuel supplies and attacks on energy infrastructure demonstrate how closely international supply chains remain connected. Changes in shipping routes can affect fuel, aviation, manufacturing, food distribution and household costs far beyond the region where a conflict occurs.

morningSummary: Good afternoon. Global energy and security concerns remain at the centre of Thursday's headlines. Only three commercial commodity vessels were recorded crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, while Brent and WTI have fallen as Saudi Arabia expands alternative crude shipments. Russia has launched a major overnight attack across Ukraine, injuring more than two dozen people according to Ukrainian officials. In Nigeria, extraordinary retail demand for the Dangote IPO has caused outages on several digital investment platforms, while the SEC is warning investors about fraud. The United States has also advanced new sanctions and tariff legislation against Russia and Iran, while Europe and Canada continue discussions about deeper strategic cooperation.
bigQuestion: With global shipping routes under pressure and energy markets still unsettled, are countries entering a period where greater self-reliance in energy and essential goods becomes a strategic necessity?
